The Ministry was established on 1 March 2024, to strengthen New Zealand’s regulatory management system and to improve regulatory quality, including the experience that New Zealanders have of complying with regulation.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">A huge congratulations to our chief executive <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/grainne-moss-2b818a?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Grainne Moss</a> on completing her final Oceans Seven swim – 41km across the Tsugaru Strait in northern Japan.

The seven iconic open water channel swims are often described as the swimming equivalent of the Seven Summits. 

Gráinne, who began this decades-long journey by swimming the English Channel at just 17 years old, has now completed them all:

1. English Channel (UK–France)
2. Cook Strait (Aotearoa New Zealand)
3. North Channel (Ireland–Scotland)
4. Molokaʻi Channel (Hawai‘i)
5. Catalina Channel (California)
6. Strait of Gibraltar (Spain–Morocco)
7. Tsugaru Strait (Japan) 

The Tsugaru Strait is widely considered one of the toughest – with strong, fast-changing currents and unpredictable conditions. And last year, Gráinne was forced to abandon her attempt of the strait due to those extreme conditions.

She now joins a very small group of swimmers to have crossed all seven straits – a feat accomplished by fewer than 50 people worldwide.

Beyond the physical challenge, this journey has always been about something bigger. Gráinne has been raising funds for <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kenzies-gift?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Kenzie's Gift</a>, a New Zealand charity supporting children and young people through grief and serious illness, providing therapy, resources and mental health support to families when they need it most.

Gráinne's goal is to raise $10,000 and she's almost there. If you’d like to support this incredible cause, you can still make a contribution. <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/edWPeu4w?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/edWPeu4w</a></p>
